content.title: About
content.content: Sour cream is a fermented dairy product made by culturing cream with lactic acid bacteria. Regular sour cream has a smooth, creamy texture, a mildly tangy flavor, and is commonly used in Russian and Eastern European cuisine as a topping, dip, or ingredient for sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional sour cream is produced from cream with a fat content of 30 % or higher.
In Russia, sour cream is considered a staple and is often served with pancakes, dumplings, and borscht.
Sour cream is available in various fat levels, from 10 % (light) to 40 % (extra‑rich).
The bacterial cultures used create probiotic benefits and give the product its characteristic tang.
It stays fresh longest when kept refrigerated at 0 °C–4 °C.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Sour cream provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamins B2 and B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Offers a modest amount of high‑quality dairy protein.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: The live cultures may help maintain a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Short‑chain fatty acids
items.content: Its fat includes short‑chain fatty acids that are easily digested.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Sour cream contains lactose, which can cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to sour cream.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Full‑fat sour cream is calorie‑dense, so it should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: Once opened, the product loses freshness quickly; proper storage is essential.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use sour cream as a topping for salads, in dips, in baked dishes, soups, and potato recipes. It can be folded into pancake batter, added to casseroles, or mixed into sauces such as a classic sour‑cream dressing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sour cream in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C in its original container or a sealed jar. After opening, consume within 5–7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may separate.
